clue.text: Projected deliveries executed

parts.note: in cricket an over is a set of six deliveries bowled from one end
a criminal executed on the gallows was hung

explanation.surface: Bowling that was carried out as planned, by the sound of a cricket commentary.
explanation.walkthrough: An OVER is the cricket term for a set of six balls bowled in a row.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that juts out above, like a ledge or cliff, is said to have projected beyond its base.

clue.text: Part of speech to girl in plant

parts.note: a verb is one of the grammatical parts of speech
Ena is a girl's name, a crossword regular

explanation.surface: A grammar lesson turns into a story about a girl among flowers.
explanation.definitionFit: Verbena is a garden flower, a genus of herbaceous perennials.

clue.text: Legal instruments?

parts.note: read as tools of the law, but a recorder is also a part-time judge in English courts, and a woodwind instrument

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a pun: 'Legal' points to judges called by this title in English courts, while 'instruments' points to the woodwind.
explanation.definitionFit: Recorders are flutes played end-on, and in England a recorder is also a barrister sitting as a part-time judge.

clue.text: United Nations port not mentioned

parts.note: Port Said is the Egyptian port at the north end of the Suez Canal

explanation.surface: A diplomatic body's harbour is quietly left out of discussion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'port' gives SAID because the Egyptian city is Port Said.
explanation.definitionFit: Words left unspoken are unsaid, a near-synonym of unvoiced.

clue.text: Europe's No 1 man in the rough got free with difficulty

indicators.note: the letters get free only with difficulty, so they are twisted out of their order

parts.note: fifteen letters, exactly the answer's

explanation.surface: A man stuck in rough ground struggles to get himself free.
explanation.walkthrough: The British king was nicknamed 'the First Gentleman of Europe' for his style and manners; 'in' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: The Prince Regent, later king, was dubbed the First Gentleman of Europe for his fashion and refinement.

clue.text: It gives protection to eastern farming policy

parts.note: CAP is the European Union's Common Agricultural Policy

explanation.surface: A protective measure shields the eastern region's agriculture.
explanation.walkthrough: CAP is the European Union's Common Agricultural Policy, long a hot topic in British politics.
explanation.definitionFit: A steel toecap is the reinforced front of a boot, guarding the toes from crushing.

clue.text: Instruction in informal conference note

parts.note: a teach-in is an informal lecture-and-discussion session, popular on campuses
G is a note of the musical scale

explanation.surface: A memo about lessons given at a casual gathering.
explanation.definitionFit: Teaching is the giving of instruction, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Artist has small apartment in one

parts.note: a cell is a small room, as in a monastery or prison
taken as written
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A painter lives alone in a tiny flat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like a container signal but supplies its own two letters; 'has' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Benvenuto Cellini was a Renaissance goldsmith and sculptor, an artist.

clue.text: School to change direction, say, and carry on

parts.note: the Perse School is an old independent school in Cambridge

indicators.note: say signals that the word for changing direction is to be heard, then spelt another way

parts.note: to veer is to change direction suddenly

explanation.surface: A school changes course and keeps going.
explanation.walkthrough: The Perse School in Cambridge is the school meant; VEER, said aloud, is spelt VERE.
explanation.definitionFit: To persevere is to keep going despite difficulty, to persist.

clue.text: Brawl makes father go to service of reconciliaton

parts.note: Fr is the abbreviation for Father, the title of a priest
ACAS is Britain's Advisory, Conciliation and Arbitration Service, which settles industrial disputes

explanation.surface: A fight sends a priest to a peace-making service.
explanation.walkthrough: ACAS is the British public body that mediates in strikes and workplace disputes; the clue's 'reconciliaton' is the page's own misspelling.
explanation.definitionFit: A fracas is a noisy quarrel or scuffle, a near-synonym of a fight.

clue.text: "Bogies spectacular, Answers ______" (The Sorcerer)

parts.note: a fill-in-the-blank quotation from the patter song of the wizard John Wellington Wells in Gilbert and Sullivan's comic opera, rhyming with spectacular

explanation.walkthrough: The Sorcerer is a Gilbert and Sullivan operetta; the missing word completes the rhyme with 'spectacular' in Wells's song about his magic wares.
explanation.definitionFit: Answers given by an oracle are prophetic, so the missing adjective describes such pronouncements.

clue.text: Knowledge acquired from 6dn?

parts.note: 6 down is the instruction a pupil receives; what the pupil gains from it is the other side of that exchange

explanation.walkthrough: 6 down is TEACHING; the answer is what the pupil gains from it.
explanation.definitionFit: Learning is knowledge gained through study, the result of being taught.

clue.text: Possibly I am the descendant of Noah

indicators.note: possibly says the letters could be arranged some other way

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether they might be descended from Noah.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possibly' rearranges IAMTHE. Ham was one of Noah's three sons.
explanation.definitionFit: A Hamite is held to descend from Ham, son of Noah, in the biblical genealogy.

clue.text: Confusion of tongues in the sort of ballad the Spanish compose

parts.note: W. S. Gilbert wrote the comic Bab Ballads
el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: Spanish composers write a ballad in a muddle of languages.
explanation.walkthrough: The Bab Ballads are W. S. Gilbert's comic verses, signed with his nickname Bab; 'in' and 'compose' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: At the Tower of Babel, God confounded the builders' language, so the name stands for a jumble of speech.

clue.text: Finance company producing music?

parts.note: brass is slang for money, the means of finance
a band is a company of people

explanation.surface: A financial firm moves into the music business.
explanation.walkthrough: BRASS is British slang for money.
explanation.definitionFit: A band of brass instruments is an ensemble that makes music, so the question mark marks a description, not a synonym.

clue.text: Put up with the Tube — it limits the pressure

parts.note: to stand something is to tolerate it
a tube is a pipe

explanation.surface: Commuters endure the London Underground under pressure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the Tube' looks like the London Underground but just means a pipe.
explanation.definitionFit: A vertical pipe open at the top acts as a relief, capping how high water pressure can rise.

clue.text: One taking action to clear ill-humour

parts.note: plain means clear, obvious
a tiff is a petty quarrel or fit of pique

explanation.surface: Someone acts to dispel a bad mood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking action' means bringing a lawsuit, not acting to fix a mood.
explanation.definitionFit: The party who brings a lawsuit against another is the one taking legal action.

clue.text: It's a drawback to dress in a cupboard

parts.note: the word draw taken backwards gives the letters for this piece
a robe is a dress or gown

explanation.surface: Keeping clothes in a cupboard has its downside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drawback' is not a disadvantage here: read it as DRAW back, giving WARD; 'in' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall cupboard for hanging clothes is a wardrobe.

clue.text: A river country's backsliders

parts.note: the Po is Italy's longest river
the States is the United States, a country; the possessive gives its final S

explanation.surface: People from a riverside nation are lapsing.
explanation.definitionFit: Apostates abandon their faith or party, falling back from former loyalty.

clue.text: Entertainment the heartless perform in a theatre

parts.note: an opera is a musical stage entertainment

indicators.note: heartless means the middle letter of the word the is removed, leaving its outside

explanation.surface: Unfeeling people put on a show at the playhouse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'theatre' suggests the stage, but the definition means surgery in an operating theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: Surgeons operate, carrying out procedures in an operating room.

clue.text: Reason for racket made by crows, say

indicators.note: say tells you the crows' noise is to be heard, not written

parts.note: crows make caws, harsh cries

explanation.surface: Someone wonders why the crows are making a din.
explanation.definitionFit: A cause is the reason behind something, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Licentious, unless having a reform

indicators.note: to reform is to form again, so these letters are reshaped

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A rake is told to mend their ways.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reform' rearranges UNLESS and A; 'having' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Sensual pleasures indulge the body, a near-synonym of lustful.

clue.text: It's odds on a fall caused it

definitions.text: It's odds on a fall caused it

parts.note: SP is the starting price, the betting odds at the off
rain is a fall of water from the sky

explanation.surface: A punter suspects the injury was almost certainly due to a tumble.
explanation.walkthrough: SP, the starting price, is the betting odds when a race begins; as a whole the clue says a fall likely caused the injury.
explanation.definitionFit: A twisted ankle or wrist, a common injury from a tumble.

clue.text: Some tennis players are broadcast

definitions.meaning: the strongest entrants in a tournament are ranked so they meet late
to broadcast is to scatter seed widely by hand

explanation.surface: Tennis stars are shown on television.
explanation.definitionFit: Top tennis players are ranked to keep them apart in the draw, and grain broadcast by hand is sown over a field.

clue.text: Pope on strange New Testament adversary

indicators.note: strange suggests the letters are in an odd, unfamiliar order

explanation.surface: The Pope comments on an odd reading of scripture, opposing it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strange' rearranges POPEON into OPPONE.
explanation.definitionFit: An opponent is one who opposes you, a direct synonym of foe.

clue.text: A club revel turns into a shambles

parts.note: a bat is a club used in sport

indicators.note: turns means the word for revel is read backwards

parts.note: a riot is a wild revel or noisy party

explanation.surface: A party at a nightclub degenerates into chaos.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns' reverses RIOT to TOIR; 'into' is a link. 'shambles' is used in its old sense, a meat market or slaughterhouse.
explanation.definitionFit: A shambles was originally a butchers' market, a slaughterhouse.

clue.text: Dislike soprani music part

indicators.note: part means a run of letters is taken from inside these words

explanation.surface: Someone is not keen on a piece of music for sopranos.
explanation.definitionFit: Animus is hostility or ill will, a close synonym of antipathy.

clue.text: Sprinkle drive and verge

parts.note: Dr is the abbreviation for Drive in street names
a verge is an edge or border

explanation.surface: Instructions for scattering seed along a driveway and its border.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sprinkle' is the cooking sense: to dredge food is to dust it with flour or sugar.
explanation.definitionFit: In cooking, to dredge is to dust food with flour or sugar.

clue.text: Small numbers of difficult peeple

definitions.meaning: as much as a hand can hold, so only a few
people hard to manage, such as unruly children

explanation.surface: A few awkward individuals.
explanation.definitionFit: A few items fit in the hand, so small quantities; troublesome children or folk are a real challenge.
